name: Per (Rich Per the Trader)
description: A wealthy, calculating dealmaker who treats people like assets and tries to buy his way out of fate, only to be undone by obsession and greed.
visualPrompt: Older Scandinavian businessman in a tailored dark coat, neat hair, sharp eyes, confident posture hiding bitterness, expensive watch, hands that look used to signing contracts and counting money, aura of control and menace

name: The Miller’s Boy
description: Sold as an infant and twice taken from his home, he grows into a capable young man whose steadiness and courage turn traps into fortune.
visualPrompt: Teen to young adult with open, trustworthy face, strong arms from mill work, simple practical clothes with worn work boots, calm expression with determined eyes, carries a small bag and a quiet resilience

name: Per’s Daughter
description: Raised under her father’s control, she is forced into a sudden marriage that ultimately becomes her escape from his grip.
visualPrompt: Young woman in modern formal wedding attire kept understated, pale but composed, hair neatly styled, expression shifting from shock to resolve, presence that suggests quiet strength

name: The Woman Taken by the Dragon
description: A kidnapped young woman living in a luxurious prison who risks everything to help the miller’s boy survive and defeat the “Dragon of Dybenfart.”
visualPrompt: Young woman in elegant but slightly tense modern clothing, pale from confinement, alert eyes, standing in a sleek glass-and-steel interior with an old ceremonial sword nearby, expression of fear turning into defiance

name: The Ferryman
description: A bent old river-crosser bound to an endless task until the curse is passed on—delivering the story’s final, merciless irony.
visualPrompt: Hunched elderly man with weathered skin and wiry strength, simple worn garments, bare hands strong from years of hauling, sharp suspicious eyes, standing knee-deep in a fast cold river
